_comment: Harness project configuration. See harness-core/docs/ai-harness-architecture.md Section 9.1 and decision-log.md H-6. The review_paths field is an extension added by H-6.10 and is not in the v2.0 architecture.
_protected_paths_comment: Absolute deny. Rewritten 7 September 2026 on the operator's instruction, once Tone Test was built and the audit needed to touch the code the old list existed to keep it away from. Almost everything here was protected for one reason: Tone Test had no business editing it. That reason has expired. What is left is protected for reasons that have not. Credentials, because they are never mine to read or write and that has nothing to do with this project's rules. decision-log.md was removed on the operator's instruction, 7 September 2026, because protecting it meant decisions reached in conversation could not be written down at the moment they were made, which is worse than the risk it guarded against. agents/ and briefs/ stay: they define how the work is done rather than record what was decided. The enforcement mechanism itself, which the operator did not ask to keep but which is included because a guard the guarded party can edit is not a guard; say so if that is not wanted. This file stays on the list, so changing it again takes the same explicit instruction that changed it this time.
_review_paths_comment: Halt and ask, rather than refuse. Re-listed 7 September 2026 by one question only: if a change here is wrong, how far does the damage reach and how long before anyone notices. The participant runners come first because the people affected are outside the organisation and cannot report a fault. Both were writable until today, which is how a query that returned nothing to every anonymous participant survived for weeks. scoring.js is here because it produces the numbers the product exists to produce and a wrong one looks exactly like a right one. csvExport.js because it is what leaves the platform. migrations because they decide who can read what, and a mistake shows as either a locked-out account or exposed data, neither obvious from the interface. style.css and App.jsx because every screen depends on them. Dropped from the old list: the operator-only builder and dashboard screens, where a mistake is visible to the person who made it within seconds, and the three authentication pages, whose commissioned work is finished.
_review_line_budget_comment: H-6.10 control one. Guidance for the Evaluator and the operator, not enforced by the hook. An edit to a review path adding more than this many lines should be questioned.
_writable_paths_comment: Everything not named above. Listed rather than implied, so a reader can see the whole picture in one file. tests/ has never existed; kept because npm run smoke and npm run spacing are the tests and they live in scripts/.
_ordering_comment: The guard checks protected_paths first, then review_paths, then writable_paths. So harness-docs/ being writable does not weaken the specific protections above it: decision-log.md, agents/ and briefs/ are all denied because protected wins. Directory-level writability avoids editing this protected file every time a task declares a new deliverable, which would put the operator in the loop for no safety gain.
_forbidden_commands_comment: Stated explicitly because the damage is not reversible. git push origin main violates H-3.5, which reserves promotion to the operator. Force push and history rewriting violate architecture Section 14.2.
_branch_comment: H-3.5. The harness works on task branches and may merge to dev. Only the operator promotes to main.
